headline.hookFact: Singapore is encouraging skills-focused employment decisions while retaining degree requirements, based on the supplied copy.
headline.readerQuestion: What can skills reveal that a degree alone cannot, and where do degrees still matter?
headline.readerParaphrase: The article asks whether current abilities increasingly matter more than university qualifications.
headline.rationale: Retains the user-supplied question as requested by the established headline preference. The reading answers the real comparison through supported learning and demonstrated abilities, while explicitly avoiding a universal claim that degrees have become unimportant.

quizzes.evidence: look more closely at what people can do
quizzes.rationale: The question tests the central skills focus in familiar words.

rejectedOptions.reason: The reading says degree study cannot show every skill; the plan considers more than the university.

rejectedOptions.option: Only the number of jobs someone had.
rejectedOptions.reason: The plan does not say only the number of previous jobs should matter.

quizzes.selectedOption: Employer-supported learning can help someone take on different responsibilities.
quizzes.evidence: his employer funded training and gave him real projects
quizzes.rationale: The training and later leadership role support new responsibilities through supported learning.

rejectedOptions.option: Studying business automatically qualifies someone for every engineering job.
rejectedOptions.reason: His business study alone is not given as automatic engineering qualification.

rejectedOptions.option: Professional training was unnecessary for his progress.
rejectedOptions.reason: Employer-funded training is explicitly part of his progress.

quizzes.selectedOption: It offers ideas without forcing companies to change their rules.
quizzes.evidence: offers guidance rather than forcing employers to change
quizzes.rationale: The framework offers guidance, preserving employer choice.

rejectedOptions.option: It requires companies to remove every degree requirement.
rejectedOptions.reason: The next sentence says degree requirements are not removed.

rejectedOptions.option: It requires companies to stop training existing workers.
rejectedOptions.reason: Training is one of the areas the framework covers, not something it prohibits.

quizzes.selectedOption: It offers guidance without compelling employers to adopt new rules.
quizzes.evidence: nor compels employers to adopt new rules
quizzes.rationale: Advisory means guidance instead of a legal mandate.

rejectedOptions.option: It legally prohibits employers from asking for qualifications.
rejectedOptions.reason: The article explicitly says it does not abolish degree requirements.

rejectedOptions.option: It requires every employer to use an identical hiring test.
rejectedOptions.reason: The 12 proposed actions are not mandatory identical testing rules.

quizzes.selectedOption: A short test cannot capture all future workplace effectiveness.
quizzes.evidence: a short test cannot reveal everything about future workplace effectiveness
quizzes.rationale: This directly states the scope limitation and does not reject tests altogether.

rejectedOptions.option: They can only measure knowledge gained at university.
rejectedOptions.reason: The article allows evidence gained outside formal education.

rejectedOptions.option: They guarantee that every candidate will be treated fairly.
rejectedOptions.reason: The article says fair assessment remains difficult, not guaranteed.

quizzes.selectedOption: Employers must make their actual selection practices consistent with that openness.
quizzes.evidence: align their actual selection practices with advertised openness
quizzes.rationale: The paragraph calls for concrete practice to match public statements.

rejectedOptions.option: Employers must stop considering every formal qualification.
rejectedOptions.reason: The text preserves the value and necessity of some formal qualifications.

rejectedOptions.option: Employers must choose applicants only from familiar universities.
rejectedOptions.reason: Selecting only familiar universities is inconsistent with openness to broader skills evidence.
